chunks: And from him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The limit of the neighbourhood (jivār) is forty houses from every side: from in front of him, and from behind him, and from his right, and from his left.

key_terms.الْجِوَارِ: Neighbourhood or the status of being a neighbour

ai.seo_question: What is the defined limit of a neighbour's jurisdiction (jivār) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the spatial extent of neighborly rights (jivār) as forty houses in all cardinal directions, a metric widely cited in Shia fiqh for determining the scope of social obligations. It reflects the practical application of maintaining communal harmony by defining the physical community where one's duties of kindness and respect are most immediate.

en.hubeali:
And from him, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The limit of the neighbourhood is forty houses from every side, from in front of him, and from behind him, and from his right, and from his left’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “
The limits of a neighborhood are forty houses on all sides, front, back, right and left.”
